source.documentName: CISCE ICSE Regulations and Syllabuses - English (Paper 1 Language & Paper 2 Literature in English)

chapters.title: Tenses and Verb Agreement
chapters.description: Rules of Simple, Continuous, Perfect, and Perfect Continuous tenses; Subject-Verb Concord across singular and compound subjects.

levels.title: Tenses in Context
levels.description: Identifying and applying appropriate tense forms in continuous passages.
subtopics: Fill in blanks with correct verb tense forms

levels.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
levels.description: Singular and plural verbs with collective nouns, either...or, neither...nor, as well as, along with.

levels.title: Chapter 1 Review & Verb Mastery
levels.description: Grammar review of tenses and verb agreement in passage format.

chapters.title: Prepositions and Phrasal Verbs
chapters.description: Prepositions of time, place, direction; fixed prepositions and idiomatic phrasal verbs.

levels.title: Prepositions of Time and Place
levels.description: Distinctions between in/at/on, since/for, between/among, beside/besides.

levels.title: Phrasal Verbs & Fixed Prepositions
levels.description: Common phrasal verbs (look after, call off, give in, put up with) and verbs taking fixed prepositions.
subtopics: Fixed prepositions with adjectives and verbs

levels.title: Chapter 2 Review & Preposition Drill
levels.description: Review of standard ICSE Question 4(b) preposition sets.

chapters.title: Sentence Transformation and Synthesis
chapters.description: Transformations using 'No sooner...than', 'Hardly...when', Active/Passive voice, Direct/Indirect speech, and degrees of comparison.

levels.title: Active and Passive Voice
levels.description: Conversion between active and passive forms across assertive, imperative, and interrogative sentences.

levels.title: Direct and Indirect Speech
levels.description: Reporting statements, questions, commands, and exclamations with reporting verb and tense shifts.

levels.title: Chapter 3 Review & Transformation Mastery
subtopics: Rewrite according to instruction without changing meaning

units.title: Literature in English (Paper 2): Drama - Julius Caesar

chapters.title: Julius Caesar: Act 1 Scene 1 & 2
chapters.description: Tribunes Flavius and Marullus chastising the plebeians; the Feast of Lupercal, the Soothsayer's warning, and Cassius tempting Brutus.

levels.title: Act 1 Scene 1: Tribunes and the Roman Mob
levels.description: Opening conflict between supporters of Pompey and the rising power of Caesar.
subtopics: Significance of the Feast of Lupercal

levels.title: Act 1 Scene 2: The Temptation of Brutus
levels.description: Cassius's psychological manipulation of Brutus, recounting Caesar's physical weaknesses in the Tiber river.
subtopics: Cassius's philosophy 'The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars'
Caesar offering the crown thrice by Antony
Brutus's inner conflict between honor and friendship

levels.title: Act 1 Contextual Extract Practice
levels.description: ICSE board pattern contextual questions on Act 1.

units.title: Literature in English (Paper 2): Treasure Chest - Prose & Poetry

chapters.title: Treasure Chest: Short Stories
chapters.description: Prescribed stories for Class 9: Bonku Babu's Friend, Oliver Asks for More, and The Model Millionaire.

levels.title: Bonku Babu's Friend (Satyajit Ray)
levels.description: Themes of timidness, bullying, and self-confidence gained through the alien Ang.
subtopics: Bonku Babu's meek nature at Sripati Majumdar's gathering
Transformation and newfound dignity of Bonku Babu

levels.title: Oliver Asks for More (Charles Dickens)
levels.description: Victorian workhouse conditions, hunger, and societal cruelty toward pauper orphans.
subtopics: The casting of lots among starving boys
Mr. Bumble's outrage at Oliver's request

levels.title: The Model Millionaire (Oscar Wilde)
levels.description: Romantic generosity vs practical materialism, featuring Hughie Erskine and Baron Hausberg.
subtopics: Hughie's charm versus lack of wealth
The sovereign given to the beggar model

chapters.title: Treasure Chest: Poems
chapters.description: Prescribed poems for Class 9: The Night Mail, Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat, and I Remember, I Remember.

levels.title: The Night Mail (W. H. Auden)
levels.description: Rhythm of the postal train travelling through Scotland, carrying letters for all social classes.
subtopics: Imagery of Scottish landscapes and sleeping cities

levels.title: Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat (T. S. Eliot)
levels.description: The indispensable railway cat maintaining order and peace on the Night Mail train.
subtopics: Duties and supervision on the train

levels.title: I Remember, I Remember (Thomas Hood)
levels.description: Contrast between childhood innocence, wonder, and the disillusionment and heavy heart of adulthood.
subtopics: Nostalgia for the sun peeping at the window
The fir trees and innocence closer to heaven
